title: Beating a retreat from where he was hit,

blocks.text: Beating a retreat from where he was hit, Sukha Singh repeatedly turned back toward the fight instead of yielding to his wound. He refused to disarm himself despite a grievous wound and kept placing himself wherever the endangered Singhs needed steadiness most.

The battle raged partly on the mountains and partly on the foothills, while the Khalsa measured their shrinking strength against a far larger enemy that was still closing from every side. Outnumbered, hungry, and trying to move horses through broken terrain, they recognized that stubbornness alone would not win the day.

A fresh resolution followed: they would scatter, preserve as many lives as possible, and return later with better preparation. The page frames that decision not as cowardice, but as a tactical withdrawal that kept the campaign alive for another round of struggle.
